To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a method for predicting catalytic residues in proteins, which we applied to a dataset of 200 proteins, and that the method was successful in identifying the catalytic residues in 70% of the proteins in the dataset, and in predicting 80% of the catalytic residues correctly.

the sequence-based prediction of the catalytic residues of enzymes is possible with high accuracy and that the prediction accuracy can be further increased by combining the prediction with a structure-based approach.

we developed a novel method for the accurate prediction of catalytic amino acids in enzymes and that the method is based on sequence similarity to a set of homologous sequences and a support vector machine (SVM) classifier.

the development of a new approach for the accurate prediction of catalytic sites in proteins.
the problem of predicting catalytic residues in proteins from sequence data.
the development of computational methods for the prediction of catalytic sites in proteins.

the sequence-based prediction of the catalytic residues is still a challenging task.

we have developed a computational tool that can predict catalytic residues in proteins with high accuracy, and that this tool is now available for use by the public.
